name: qa_ratepitch
title: OS-RATEPITCH, rows QA-SLD-007..009 of docs/qa/catalogue/sample_load.md: samples that are not 44,100 Hz play at the pitch of their recorded rate (measured over the USB AUDIO capture)

steps.say: OS-RATEPITCH (bug fix). A sample must play at the pitch of its recorded rate. Needs the USB AUDIO device (usb mode audio, profile 8: the capture channel of MASTER L is 7; with another profile pass --var CH=<n> --var CHANNELS=<count>) and the maintainer's test files at the card ROOT (/8SVX, /AIFF; PC copy build-sdtest/O3TEST, never committed). The default pad board: pad 12 is note 60, the root note.

steps.note: precondition: the unit presents USB AUDIO
(instrument 2 is the load target of QA-RP-001: a pad on the Instrument screen picks it)
RESCAN
UP to the root (the list keeps the last folder)
(the cursor to the first entry)
select the 8SVX folder by name (OS-HILNAV: the state line's sel; a count of Down presses breaks when the card holds one more file)
F3 enters 8SVX
(the cursor to the first entry)
select gen-loop-16726.8svx by name (OS-HILNAV: the state line's sel; a count of Down presses breaks when the card holds one more file)
F1 LOAD
loaded; no PITCH IS OFF warning any more
on Sample Load a pad picks an instrument: leave it for Pattern before the note
the root note (60), held: the sample loops
qa_rp_001: 16726 / 128 = 130.7 Hz. Before the fix this sounded at 345 Hz (+17 semitones). A failure line shows the pitch that was heard
(instrument 3 for the 44,100 Hz control)
UP to the root
(the cursor to the first entry)
select the AIFF folder by name (OS-HILNAV: the state line's sel; a count of Down presses breaks when the card holds one more file)
F3 enters AIFF
(the cursor to the first entry)
select gen-24bit-loop.aif by name (OS-HILNAV: the state line's sel; a count of Down presses breaks when the card holds one more file)
on Sample Load a pad picks an instrument: leave it for Pattern before the note
qa_rp_002: a 44,100 Hz sample is unchanged: 689.1 Hz

steps.say: QA-RP-003, by ear: load /8SVX/ff_mensaje_22095.8svx (22,095 Hz speech, 1.33 s) into another instrument and tap pad 12 (note 60). It must sound as a natural speaking voice, not an octave high and not squeaky; it lasts about 1.3 s. Then load /AIFF/gen-aifc-sowt.aifc (22,050 Hz, a short 344.5 Hz tone) and tap pad 12: a low, short beep, an octave below the 44,100 Hz control (689 Hz) of the step above. Report what you heard.

QA-RP-004, optional, Sample edit: on the 22,050 Hz instrument open Sample edit and run AMIGA 8287; the converted sample, now on the Amiga voice, must sound at the same pitch (344.5 Hz) as before the conversion, because the conversion resamples from the sample's own rate.
